entries.title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
entries.summary: OpenAI announces $2 million commitment to research on AI and children's safety, supporting development of shared tools to measure risks and opportunities for young people.

entries.title: Record number of cyber incidents reported to UK privacy regulator
entries.summary: UK organisations reported record cyber incidents to the data protection regulator this year. Cybersecurity firms attribute surge to data extortion and artificial intelligence-driven attacks.

entries.title: Microsoft outage: Impact shows risk of M365 bundle lock-in
entries.summary: Global Microsoft Exchange outage disrupted UK government departments, hospitals, schools and police forces, preventing email transmission. NHS, councils and other organisations reported service disruptions but maintained critical functions.

entries.title: Iranian Hacks With Russian Characteristics
entries.summary: Covers alleged Iranian hacking operations exhibiting characteristics associated with Russian threat actors.

entries.title: Poor AI can compound investigative biases and add to cognitive overload, putting justice at risk, warns white paper
entries.summary: White paper warns that poorly implemented AI in investigations can reinforce investigative biases, increase cognitive overload, and jeopardise justice outcomes.

entries.title: The Effectiveness of Russian Nuclear Signaling in the Ukraine War
entries.summary: Evaluates effectiveness of Russian nuclear signalling during Ukraine war and examines implications for broader international nuclear dynamics.

entries.title: Court Lets Florida Age Verification Demands on Meta Proceed
entries.summary: Florida appeals court refused to dismiss state attorney general's lawsuit against Meta requiring age verification for all Floridian users. Court ruled Section 230 provides limited, not absolute, immunity and found no First Amendment violation yet.

entries.title: TSMC confirms employee data breach tied to cloud service provider
entries.summary: TSMC confirms employee data breach via compromised cloud service provider. Investigation found no TSMC systems breached; stolen data unrelated to company operations or customer information.

entries.title: Ransomware attack on Belarusian cloud firm disrupts businesses for days
entries.summary: Belarusian cloud firm ActiveCloud suffered a ransomware attack where hackers breached systems and encrypted cloud infrastructure, preventing customers from accessing key services for several days.

entries.title: What’s really at stake in the Jensen Huang saga
entries.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned. The article discusses broader implications including Nvidia's China dealings, US government protection of the company, AI industry stability, and mentions Megaspeed, with full details promised in extended coverage.

entries.title: AI Kill Switches: What Policymakers Should Know
entries.summary: Examines AI kill switches—emergency shutdown systems that rapidly halt AI operations during harmful incidents. Describes implementation at multiple intervention levels from hardware to software, with varying scope from surgical to broad effects. Notes policymakers should consider collateral damage trade-offs when designing shutdown requirements.

entries.title: AI agents bring down wind farm within two hours
entries.summary: Reports that two off-the-shelf large language models successfully hacked a replicated wind farm, disabling six turbines producing nearly 10MW within two hours using only VPN credentials. Demonstrates attackers need not possess specialist operational technology knowledge to compromise critical infrastructure.

entries.title: Why the use of AI by the UK’s intelligence services needs independent oversight
entries.summary: Argues UK intelligence agencies use advanced AI tools in secret for mass surveillance, gathering and processing unprecedented data on populations. Calls for urgent independent oversight, citing the Pentagon's reported interest in using AI for bulk data collection on Americans and foreign actors weaponising AI for surveillance.

entries.title: Checking Ai Output In Police Open-Source Investigations: A Step-By-Step Methodological Review
entries.summary: Methodological review examining potential problems and benefits when AI tools are used in police open-source investigations, and which checks protect investigations against risks whilst remaining open to unexpected advantages.

entries.title: Instrument Or Power: How Academic Abstracts Represent Artificial Intelligence In Intelligence And Police Work
entries.summary: Examines how academic abstracts represent artificial intelligence entering intelligence and police work, including criminal intelligence supporting investigations and anticipatory intelligence for prevention, and how academic framing may influence perceptions of associated risks.

entries.title: 354 dark web vendors and buyers arrested in Europol-coordinated global crackdown
entries.summary: Europol-coordinated operation across fourteen countries arrested 354 dark web vendors and buyers involved in cybercrime, drug trafficking and firearms offences. Operation TorNado ran from May 2025 to October 2026, conducting hundreds of house searches globally.

entries.title: 6.4 million victim datasets secured in international operation against malware networks
entries.summary: Europol and international partners dismantled criminal infrastructure behind Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC malware networks. Law enforcement seized 235 servers and 257 domains, securing 6.4 million victim datasets and severely disrupting malware distribution operations.

entries.title: Meme-To-Radicalisation Pipeline: Unpacking the Jihadist-Themed Edgy Humour on Indonesian TikTok and Instagram
entries.summary: Analyses how unaffiliated Indonesian social media creators inadvertently normalise ISIS content by disguising jihadist footage and nasheeds as satirical memes blending socio-economic grievances with extremist aesthetics. Contends this grey area creates radicalisation pathways for youth despite creators lacking genuine ideological ties to ISIS.

entries.title: Global Microsoft outage leaves users open to phishing attacks
entries.summary: Global Microsoft outage caused service degradation across multiple platforms including Outlook, Teams, Exchange Online, and Intune. Outage creates security risks, potentially enabling phishing and unauthorised system access, though Microsoft reported no malicious activity at time of writing.

entries.title: Bug-hunting time cut dramatically with AI, says Forescout
entries.summary: Forescout research finds AI dramatically accelerates vulnerability discovery in critical infrastructure code, compressing research timescales and reducing costs for both security researchers and attackers. AI changes economics of vulnerability discovery but does not eliminate need for expert researchers.
